condition: Pulmonary embolism presenting as a raised D-dimer
summary: 45-year-old woman recalled for a D-dimer of 1450 µg/L FEU taken for pleuritic chest pain after a long-haul flight.

inputs.hpi: Recalled after the out-of-hours doctor's blood test: D-dimer raised. Three days of sharp left-sided chest pain on breathing in and breathlessness on stairs, since a 10-hour flight. On the combined pill. No cough, no fever, no leg swelling noticed.

exam.general: Mildly breathless. HR 106, BP 124/78, RR 22, SpO2 95% on air.

guideline.name: NICE NG158 Venous thromboembolic diseases
guideline.section: 1.1: two-level PE Wells score; D-dimer when PE unlikely; CTPA when likely or D-dimer positive

rationale: Entry point: a laboratory result. The D-dimer alone is non-specific; the loop goes back to the history (pleuritic pain, flight, oestrogen) and the examination (tachycardia, tachypnoea) and asks for the Wells score.

authoring.author: Claude (vademecum phase 1, entry-point pilot)
authoring.notes: Starts from a result (laboratory, imaging or pathology), not a complaint. Written for the vademecum shadow (clinval:web --engine vademecum); not verified on iOS; clinical sign-off pending (docs/clinical-validation/changes/vademecum-phase1.md).
